standard_prerequisites.name: Tensor product of dg modules over a dg algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a dg algebra A and dg modules M over A and N over A, the tensor product M tensor_A N is a dg module whose differential satisfies the signed Leibniz rule on decomposable tensors.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both displayed differentials and their expansions rest on that rule (source lines 4974-4989).

standard_prerequisites.name: Differential of a homogeneous module homomorphism
standard_prerequisites.statement: For homogeneous f : M -> M' of degree n the differential in the Hom complex is d of M' composed with f minus the signed composition of f with d of M.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the shape of the differential of f and of f tensor the identity, which the proof compares (source lines 4970-4981).

standard_prerequisites.name: Induced functors on the module and homotopy categories
standard_prerequisites.statement: A functor of dg categories compatible with differentials induces functors between the module categories and their homotopy categories (the author's lemma lemma-functorial, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is invoked in the statement to pass from the dg functor to the functors on Mod and K(Mod) (source line 4962).

core_obligations: Reduce to compatibility: note that the construction is already a functor of the underlying graded categories, so it remains to check compatibility with differentials (source lines 4966-4968).

Write both differentials: for a homogeneous A-module homomorphism f of degree n write d(f) and d(f tensor id_N) in the standard form using the differentials of the source and target (source lines 4968-4981).

Evaluate on a decomposable tensor and cancel: apply the second formula to x tensor y with x and y homogeneous, expand both terms using the tensor-product Leibniz rule, cancel the two copies of the signed f(x) tensor d_N(y) term, and conclude d(f) tensor id_N equals d(f tensor id_N), which is the compatibility (source lines 4982-4994).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the claim to compatibility with differentials.
Write the differentials of f and of f tensor id_N in the standard signed shape.
Evaluate on x tensor y, cancel the common signed term, and conclude the compatibility.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-tensor at source lines 4944-4963: for a ring R, dg algebras (A,d) and (B,d) over R and a dg (A,B)-bimodule N, the construction sending a dg A-module M to M tensor over A with N is a functor of dg categories, and hence induces functors on the module category and on the homotopy category. The proof at source lines 4965-4995 is the sign computation that makes the functor compatible with differentials: it recalls the differential of a homogeneous A-module homomorphism f of degree n, writes the differential of f tensor the identity of N in the same shape, applies both sides to a decomposable tensor x tensor y with x and y homogeneous, expands the two terms using the Leibniz-type rules for the tensor product differential, and observes that the two copies of the signed term f(x) tensor d_N(y) cancel, leaving exactly d(f)(x) tensor y. The whole content is that cancellation, which needs the sign (-1)^(n + deg x) to be produced by the tensor-product differential in both terms; the statement records none of it. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
